description: Run a shell command inside a vernam broker session (same as `vn run -- sh -c COMMAND`) and return its exit code, stdout and stderr. Each API key is in the environment under its own name as a placeholder token (vn_...), and API base URLs point at the local proxy, which swaps in the real key on the way out. The real API keys never reach the command. Secrets marked as plain (target "(plain env var: agents can read it)") are readable by design: commands run through vernam get their real values. API keys are brokered: commands only ever get placeholder tokens. Output is capped at 64 KB per stream. The command runs as the user, on their machine.

command.description: Shell command, run with /bin/sh -c. Reference keys as $NAME, e.g. curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" "$OPENAI_BASE_URL/models".

cwd.description: Working directory (absolute path). Default: where the MCP server was started.

env.description: vernam environment. Default: VERNAM_ENV, then the nearest .vernam.json, then dev.

timeoutSeconds.description: Kill the command after this long. Default 120.

name: vernam_run
title: Run a command with brokered keys
